goal: Learn creator causal rationale by verifying the actual visual BEFORE/AFTER and cross-family stage review, rather than measuring the finished typeface or blindly modifying glyph widths.

original_maker_explains.condition: Repeated Chinese structural components across dozens/hundreds of glyphs can accumulate systematic visual proportion errors that are not visible while looking at one glyph alone.
original_maker_explains.action: Conduct multi-person and multi-stage review; resolve the shareable radical's proportion and contour.
original_maker_explains.evidence: Article explicitly captions a revision of 阝 on 那 and shows red BEFORE, cyan AFTER. The same studio documents having to reverse a too-wide 口 radical after expansion to thousands of characters.
original_maker_explains.review_stages: prototype ~10–20, then cross-glyph reviews around 300, 1,000, 3,000 characters
original_maker_explains.separate_example: 包 is explicitly reworked depending on location in 包/胞/雹/炰/庖/袌; not a single component stamp copied identically.

empirical_source.numeric_precision: LOW; independent color segmentation and thumbnail normalization, NOT recovered human vector paths, cannot treat 13.26% as actual param delta or aesthetic uplift.

family_original_photo.source_caption: Publisher-labeled before vs after glyph family grid

what_can_be_supported: Actual published same-glyph visual differences, not merely multiple finished styles.
The overall visual frame and colored ink counts can remain near constant while localized contours change in a way selected by the designer.
The maker explicitly documents proportion revision of 阝 and long-tail systemic review of reused radicals.
cannot_claim: The author intended exactly 13.26 percent pixels changed, or used that value as a rule.
Color-thresholded pixel overlap proves improved aesthetics.
The author's brush pressure, speed, bezier control history or exact source edits are known.
An expert sans/serif typography principle transfers unmodified to expressive 六島-like dry-brush logotypes.
Any new Chinese character has actually been generated via this method or preferred in a blind user comparison.

candidate_action.label: 同部件多字审查→局部轮廓修订→保留整体形态→族内复核
prerequisites: At least two source-published stages of exactly the same original glyph and identifiable target component.
Check glyph position, radical role, and family context instead of one stroke direction.
Visual reviewer must actually diagnose a systematic imbalance across more than one glyph before changing shapes.
proposed_causal_sequence: Determine whether the problem is local contour or systematic radical allocation, based on maker-side documented examples.
Alter only the localized component geometry/negative space, not default uniform scale of all glyph components.
Retain legible whole-glyph footprint and original stroke identity as constraints rather than objective maxima.
Re-evaluate the entire affected glyph group at matching sizes and repeated text contexts; reject improvements that are only numeric.

source_classification_corrections.reason: DFA award page does not establish p09 as an attributable chronologically matched before/after glyph pair.
Separate cross-source evidence; cannot merge source pixel statistics into Typotheque same-artist family.
C80/standard variant not proven to be chronological edit stages.

next: No more B/C minor geometric edits. Need a full author-documented sketch/creative intermediate/finished expressive CJK lettering sequence with the same glyph(s), then compare candidate mechanism on unseen texts by human preference; if missing, report observational limitation instead of pretending to learn expressive design.
